hero.headline: Jensen Beach Park restrooms and cafe rebuild expected by late 2027
hero.teaser: Beachgoers at Jensen Beach Park are waiting for the rebuild of the park's restrooms and concession building destroyed in a fire on New Year's Eve in December 2024. The county says the new Sea Turtle Beach Cafe will seat 100 people with 33 bar seats.
hero.body:
Beachgoers at Jensen Beach Park are waiting for the rebuild of the park's restrooms and concession building, which was destroyed in a fire on New Year's Eve in December 2024. The site is currently an empty plot of land, leaving visitors with limited facilities during what is typically peak season for the popular beach destination.

Beachgoer Gonda Ghebert reached out to WPTV expressing frustration that visitors are left with only one very small restroom facility to serve the entire beach, which has become increasingly unreasonable during weekends, holidays, and peak tourist season. Regular visitors say they also miss the cafe that once provided convenient access to food and drinks. Julie Goings, who frequents the beach, said the previous facility offered nice, clean restrooms and showers, and it was convenient being able to get a snack or drink right off the deck. Sam Elliott noted that the only thing really missing is concessions and food availability.

Kevin Abbate, the Parks and Recreation director, says the permitting process takes time because the project sits on a protected dune and must go through the Department of Environmental Protection. That permit is currently in process. The design for the new 9,000 square foot Sea Turtle Beach Cafe is 80 percent complete. The building will be about 15 feet in elevation with 100 seats and 33 at the bar. Final funding is expected to be approved in September.

The county hopes to start construction in early 2027 with a completion goal of late 2027, just in time for the winter season. The county told WPTV they do not have any plans for additional temporary restrooms or facilities in the meantime. Abbate says the cafe will be worth the wait, explaining that the county wants to do it right and that designing it properly will result in fewer issues and a much smoother construction process. Beachgoers say they are anxiously awaiting construction, hoping it moves quickly and looking forward to having the bathrooms up and running along with another convenient spot for refreshments.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce rethinks waterfront development process after multiple lawsuits
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of Little J.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of the historic Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant. The rejection means more taxpayer dollars will likely go toward defending the case. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the settlement was not practical, particularly a provision that would have required taxpayers to vote on future waterfront land decisions. Broderick told WPTV he feels the lawsuit does not have any merit but acknowledged some controversies mentioned in the lawsuit, which allege a broader pattern of defective administration of city waterfront properties.

The Little Jim's case is at least the fourth waterfront property dispute WPTV has reported on and the second to result in a lawsuit. In 2023, developer Dale Matteson of King's Landing threatened legal action after claiming the city sold him buildable land filled with old power plant concrete. In 2024, developer Chris Shelli of Fisherman's Wharf filed suit after state records showed the city promised property it did not own. In 2025, the city abruptly canceled the bidding process for Little Jim's land lease amid public outcry, prompting Keene's lawsuit. This year, the city became responsible for nearly $200,000 in unpaid rent tied to Crabby's Waterfront Restaurant. Broderick said Fort Pierce will take a top down, bottom up approach to examine the entirety of the city's property portfolio and fix issues one asset at a time. The city is creating a new real estate management position to track leases, rent payments, and waterfront properties.

cards.headline: 66-year-old Fort Pierce man dead after shooting on Essex Drive in St. Lucie County
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified the victim in Tuesday afternoon's shooting on Essex Drive as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce. Deputies responded around 3:30 p.m. to a home in the 2700 block of Essex Drive after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned an adult man had shot another adult man with a rifle.

Deputies took the suspect into custody and began providing emergency medical care to Barnes until St. Lucie County Fire District personnel arrived. Barnes was then taken to a local hospital, where he died. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division are continuing to process evidence, conduct interviews, and work to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The suspect remains in custody. Investigators say there is no threat to the public. This is an ongoing investigation.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce overhauls development process after multiple waterfront lawsuits
cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant. The rejection means more taxpayer dollars will likely go toward defending the case. Keene told WPTV he will continue the litigation and fight. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the settlement was not practical, particularly a provision requiring taxpayer votes on future waterfront land decisions. Broderick also said he feels the lawsuit does not have merit, though the city has an obligation to defend it.

The Little Jim's case is at least the fourth waterfront property dispute reported by WPTV and the second to result in a lawsuit. In 2023, King's Landing developer Dale Matteson threatened legal action after claiming the city sold him buildable land filled with old power plant concrete. In 2024, Fisherman's Wharf developer Chris Shelli filed suit after state records showed the city promised property it did not own. In 2025, the city abruptly canceled a bid process for Little Jim's after public outcry, prompting Keene's lawsuit and leaving developers Luigi and Drita Lucaj frustrated. This year, the city became responsible for nearly $200,000 in unpaid rent tied to Crabby's Waterfront Restaurant.

Broderick acknowledged controversies mentioned in the lawsuit, which allege a broader pattern of defective administration of city waterfront properties. When asked about allegations of mismanaging waterfront properties, Broderick said he would not say the properties are managed poorly but rather that they are not being managed at all, calling it an issue he takes very seriously. Broderick said fixing the problems will require a top down, bottom up approach to examine the entire portfolio and fix assets one at a time.

The city is creating a new real estate management position to track leases, rent payments, and waterfront properties with the goal of preventing future problems. Broderick said he will not rest until he gets to the bottom of the issue and categorizes all properties in spreadsheets. Both sides remain open to negotiating, with Keene saying he wants transparency rather than money and is willing to revise his offer. Broderick said he will consider any feasible settlement that keeps the case out of court.

cards.headline: Messi leads Argentina to stunning 3-2 comeback over Egypt to reach World Cup quarterfinals
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and led Argentina to an improbable 3-2 victory over Egypt on Tuesday after trailing by two goals with only 11 minutes left in regulation time.
cards.body:
Argentina trailed 2-0 on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico before mounting one of the great World Cup comebacks. Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute, followed by Messi's equalizer in the 83rd minute that brought his World Cup goal total to a record-extending 21. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete the comeback.

Messi was in tears after the final whistle. He had earlier missed a penalty kick that was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir in the first half and later hit the post when the score was 1-0. The 39-year-old forward's performance came in what might be the last of his six World Cups. Messi has now missed four of eight penalty kicks at World Cup tournaments.

The defending champions will next face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said after the match he was emotional about what the group of players accomplished.

cards.headline: 28-year-old man dies after weekend double shooting on South 14th Street in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was shot multiple times in Fort Pierce over the weekend. The shooting happened early Sunday morning at about 3:43 a.m. in the 300 block of South 14th Street.
cards.body:
A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was shot multiple times in Fort Pierce over the weekend. The shooting happened early Sunday morning at about 3:43 a.m. in the 300 block of South 14th Street. Police said officers arrived at the scene and found two people with apparent gunshot wounds. The man sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was taken to a local hospital but died from his injuries on Tuesday. Officers also found a 28-year-old woman with injuries to her hand from the shooting, but her injuries were described as not life-threatening. The names of the victims have not been released.

Police said a preliminary investigation indicated that the victims had been involved in an earlier altercation in the 5800 block of Okeechobee Road before returning to their residence. As they arrived home, police said a man believed to be involved in the previous altercation approached and opened fire before fleeing the area. Police said this investigation remains active and ongoing. Anyone with information in the case is encouraged to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Clerk's website goes down for hours after redirection issue
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday morning before coming back online around 1:30 p.m.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website went down for hours Tuesday morning, redirecting visitors to another site before coming back online by about 1:30 p.m. Clerk and Comptroller Michelle Miller posted a video on social media Tuesday afternoon assuring the public that no personal or confidential information was compromised or at risk. Miller said the clerk's office does not store sensitive personal information on the public-facing website and that the website faced a temporary redirection issue caused by a third-party service provider.

Jose Clavijo, the agency's IT director, said they received a report just before 8 a.m. that something was wrong with the county clerk's homepage. Clavijo said as soon as he identified the issue, he turned the website off and started an investigation. The clerk's office communications team said this was not a hack because no personal information was compromised. Residents could still access information and services on the website through direct links instead of using the homepage. Clavijo said payments, property fraud services, and all other services remained available. He said the office is working to prevent similar issues and that there will be a tremendous remediation once they identify the exact issue.

hero.headline: Trump called FIFA president to get Balogun red card suspension lifted before U.S. World Cup match
hero.teaser: President Donald Trump intervened on behalf of American forward Folarin Balogun, calling FIFA president Gianni Infantino to request a review of the red card that would have suspended him from the Belgium match.
hero.body:
President Donald Trump intervened on behalf of American star forward Folarin Balogun, whose red-card suspension was lifted in a decision that allows him to play in a World Cup match against Belgium on Monday. Balogun received a red card for stepping awkwardly on the right ankle of Tarik Muharemović of Bosnia-Herzegovina in a 2-0 round of 32 win on Wednesday, triggering an automatic one-game suspension. FIFA announced Sunday that the suspension had been lifted for the round of 16 match, an extraordinary move that appeared to be the first time since 1962 that a red card during a World Cup did not result in a suspension. Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino after the game asking FIFA review the red card, according to a person familiar with the call who spoke on condition of anonymity because the person was not authorized to speak publicly about the matter.

The Royal Belgian Football Association said it was astonished by the decision and is investigating all potential options to challenge it. Belgium coach Rudi Garcia mocked FIFA's action, saying he didn't know that in FIFA's offices the fifth of July was the first of April in Europe, making an April Fools' Day comparison. U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino defended the decision, saying the team was punished enough against Bosnia-Herzegovina to play with 10 men for 30 minutes in a decision that was completely unfair. Balogun's three goals matched Landon Donovan in 2010 for the second-most goals by an American in a World Cup, behind only Bert Patenaude's four in 1930.

cards.headline: International Olympic Committee ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 LA Olympics
cards.teaser: The IOC advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
cards.body:
The IOC advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The move was expected since the International Olympic Committee advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity. The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension were imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine.

Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem, saying that decision will come at an appropriate time. The IOC said to address the lack of confidence in the global sporting community relating to the return of Russian athletes to international competition, those athletes must give multiple doping controls and be part of a recognized testing program. The IOC said it will continue to not organize IOC events in Russia or invite Russian government or state officials to its events. The next Olympic competition is the 2026 Youth Summer Games in Dakar, Senegal opening Oct. 31.

cards.headline: United States eliminated from World Cup after 4-1 loss to Belgium in round of 16
cards.body:
The United States' hopes for a deep World Cup run at home ended when Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium expose the Americans' defensive liabilities in a 4-1 win Monday night at Lumen Field that earned a quarterfinal berth. Goalkeeper Matt Freese's gaffe gave the Red Devils a third goal early in the second half, and second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku added Belgium's final goal in the third minute of stoppage time. Seeking its first World Cup title, Belgium knocked the U.S. out in the round of 16 for the second time in 12 years and extended its unbeaten streak to 18 games. The Red Devils play 2010 champion Spain on Friday at Inglewood, California, for a semifinal berth against France or Morocco.

Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 midway through the first half with his second free kick goal of the tournament, energizing a largely red-white-and-blue crowd of 66,925, but the Americans conceded just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff. American star Christian Pulisic could only watch from the bench after injuring his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt and was replaced seven minutes later. After winning three games in a World Cup for the first time in this expanded 48-nation tournament, the U.S. failed in its quest to reach the quarterfinals for the first time since 2002 and lost to Belgium for the seventh straight time since a victory at the initial tournament in 1930.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Roll Past Jupiter 11-2 in Series Opener
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets opened their road series against the Jupiter Hammerheads with an 11-2 rout Tuesday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium, leading from the first pitch to the las
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets opened their road series against the Jupiter Hammerheads with an 11-2 rout Tuesday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium, leading from the first pitch to the last.

Leadoff hitter Antonio Jimenez set the tone immediately, homering on the very first pitch of the game from Jupiter starter Jonas Uzcategui. Jimenez finished the night 4 for 6 with the home run, two doubles, four runs scored and two stolen bases. He came a triple short of the cycle, striking out and hitting into a fielder's choice in his final two at-bats.

Four St. Lucie pitchers held the Hammerheads to just two hits. Starter Jose Lopez, making his team debut, worked four solid innings, allowing one hit and two runs with four walks and four strikeouts. Relievers Zack Mack, Miguel Mejias and Elwis Mijares combined for five innings of one-hit relief. Mack earned the win.

The Mets built a 3-0 lead through two innings before Jupiter answered with two runs and put the tying run on third base in the fourth. Lopez escaped the jam by getting Edgardo De Leon to pop out, preserving a 3-2 lead.

St. Lucie broke the game open with four runs in the sixth. Branny De Oleo drove in a run with a single, Jimenez scored on a wild pitch, and AJ Salgado added a two-run single to push the lead to 7-2.

The Mets tacked on two unearned runs in the eighth on a Jupiter error and another run-scoring wild pitch, then closed the scoring in the ninth on a De Oleo RBI single and yet another wild pitch that brought Jimenez home.

De Oleo went 2 for 5 with three RBI and Salgado added two hits and two RBI. Julio Zayas drew four walks, while Jeremy Rodriguez walked twice and scored two runs.

The win improved St. Lucie to 8-2 at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium this season and marked its third straight victory over Jupiter. The Mets (4-10, 37-43) and Hammerheads (5-11, 42-40) continue their series Wednesday, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Leon County judge sets July hearing on lawsuit challenging Fishback's eligibility in Florida governor's race
hero.body:
A Leon County judge set aside two days later this month to decide whether Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement to run for governor. Judge David Frank scheduled the matter for July 21 and 22 during a Tuesday scheduling hearing, warning attorneys there is an extreme shortage of time with the Aug. 18 primary approaching. The lawsuit was filed by Lt. Jay Collins, one of Fishback's rivals in the GOP primary, who argues Fishback does not meet the state's residency requirement. Collins' complaint points to records tied to Fishback's voter registration and residency in Washington, D.C.

Frank noted it is likely already too late to stop ballots from being printed. He explained that if Fishback is disqualified, there would be an injunction to the Department of State directing supervisors of elections not to count votes for Fishback and to post a notice. Fishback's attorney, former state representative Anthony Sabatini, told the judge the case turns on more than paperwork, arguing Fishback's intent will be central to determining residency. Sabatini said the defense wants time to present witnesses and documents. Witness and exhibit lists are due five days before the July 21 hearing.

The courtroom fight comes just days after the issue spilled onto the debate stage. During last week's GOP primary debate, Fishback, Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner appeared together. Frontrunner Byron Donalds skipped the event but still loomed large over the debate, with his rivals repeatedly invoking him and his position in the race. Fishback pressed Collins directly over the lawsuit, getting the lieutenant governor to note his Florida roots. Fishback said during the debate, "Case closed. Drop the lawsuit." He later accused Collins of trying to steal the election with Byron Donalds. Collins pushed back, saying the challenge belongs in court. "That is a matter for the court," Collins said. "I actually respect the judicial system."

For now, Fishback remains on the ballot. The case adds uncertainty to the primary calendar at a time when election officials are already preparing ballots and candidates are running out of time to shift the race. Even if Fishback is removed, the broader GOP contest may still revolve around Donalds, who has maintained a commanding position in the primary through polling, fundraising and endorsements. Axios reported Tuesday that Donalds continues to tower over the field as the Aug. 18 primary approaches.

cards.headline: FDA recalls frozen Publix GreenWise organic blueberries sold in Florida and seven other states over E. coli contamination
cards.teaser: The Food and Drug Administration issued a recall for frozen Publix GreenWise Organic Blueberries due to possible E. coli contamination. The product was shipped to Publix retail stores throughout Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Virginia.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration has issued a recall for frozen Publix GreenWise Organic Blueberries due to possible E. coli contamination. The product, GreenWise Organic IQF Blueberries 10 oz, was shipped to Publix retail stores throughout eight states, including Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Virginia. The affected product has lot code 60401 and a best by date of February 9, 2028. Consumers who purchased these blueberries are asked not to consume them and should discard them or return them to the place of purchase for a full refund. The FDA has reported 12 confirmed cases of consumers experiencing stomach illness between May 11, 2026 and June 5, 2026 linked with E. coli infections.

Those who have consumed food contaminated with E. coli can experience severe stomach cramps, diarrhea (which may be bloody), and vomiting. Most healthy individuals can recover within a week; however, some infections can result in serious health complications. Consumers with questions or concerns about the recall can contact Info.foodsafety@comfrut.com or 336-899-5612.

cards.headline: Median-income Florida households need 17 months longer to save for home down payment than a decade ago
cards.teaser: A new study by Smart Asset found that it now takes the median-income household earner in Florida 17 months longer to save up for a down payment in 2026 than in 2016. For Floridians earning minimum wage, the burden is far greater.
cards.body:
A new study by Smart Asset found that it now takes the median-income household earner in Florida 17 months longer to save up for a down payment in 2026 than in 2016. For Floridians who earn a minimum wage of $14 an hour, it takes nearly 26 years to save up for a down payment on a home. Florida ranked No. 25 on the list.

Residents in Idaho have been affected the most in the last 10 years, now needing 40 months longer to buy a home than in 2016. Only in three states can median-income households save a down payment faster than they could in 2016: Louisiana, Mississippi and North Dakota. West Virginia has the nation's lowest down payment burden, with a median-income household needing 5.5 years to save for a down payment in 2026, just three months longer than in 2016. The study found that saving for a down payment on a minimum-wage income alone is essentially impossible in every state.

cards.headline: Marion County alligator attack forces amputation of 11-year-old Pennsylvania boy's right hand
cards.teaser: An 11-year-old boy is recovering at home in Pennsylvania after an alligator attack in Marion County resulted in the amputation of his right hand. The boy and his father were fishing at Nelson's Fish Camp near Umatilla when the incident happened two weekends ago.
cards.body:
Brodie and his father were visiting from Pennsylvania and fishing two weekends ago at Nelson's Fish Camp near Umatilla when the incident happened. Andrew Wright, one of Brodie's relatives, said the two were aware of their surroundings and had seen alligators in the area, but nothing that was close to them or of concern. The alligator came out of nowhere as Brodie was putting a fish back in the water that he had just reeled in. The alligator grabbed Brodie by the arm, and his dad jumped on it, hoping to pry its mouth open. When he did that, the gator did its roll, and it broke pretty much every bone in Brodie's lower arm, severing part of his hand.

At the hospital, doctors had to amputate Brodie's right hand, which Wright said is his dominant one when playing sports like baseball and football. Wright said physically and emotionally, it's going to be a very long road for Brodie. Despite what's ahead, Brodie remains in good spirits, as shown by his smile in photos taken after the attack. A GoFundMe for Brodie and his family had already raised more than $19,000 in donations as of Tuesday morning. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission said it captured and killed the nearly 9-foot alligator believed to be responsible for the attack.

hero.headline: Jensen Beach Park restrooms and concession building won't reopen until late 2027
hero.body:
Beachgoers at Jensen Beach Park are waiting for the rebuild of the park's restrooms and concession building, which was destroyed in a fire on New Year's Eve in December 2024. The site is currently an empty plot of land, leaving beachgoers with only one very small restroom facility to serve the entire beach.

Gonda Ghebert, who reached out to WPTV, wrote that the situation has become increasingly unreasonable during weekends, holidays, and peak tourist season. Those who frequent the beach say they also miss the cafe. Julie Goings, who visits regularly, said the former facility had nice, clean showers and it was convenient coming off the deck to get a snack or a drink. Sam Elliott said the only thing really missing is concessions and food availability.

Kevin Abbate, the Parks and Recreation director, says the permitting process takes time because the building sits on a protected dune and must go through the Department of Environmental Protection. That permit is currently in process. The design for the new 9,000 square foot Sea Turtle Beach Cafe is 80 percent complete. The new facility will stand about 15 feet in elevation and include 100 seats and 33 at the bar. Abbate says the cafe will be worth the wait, explaining that designing it properly means fewer issues and a smoother construction process.

The county expects final funding approval in September 2026. They hope to start construction in early 2027 with a completion goal of late 2027, just in time for the winter season. The county has no plans for additional temporary restrooms or facilities in the meantime. Those who use the beach say they are anxiously awaiting its construction, with Elliott hoping it moves real fast and Goings saying she wants the bathrooms up and running and would appreciate another convenient spot.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man, 66, killed in shooting on Essex Drive, suspect in custody
hero.body:
Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce died Tuesday after being shot at a home in the 2700 block of Essex Drive, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Deputies responded around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound.

When deputies arrived, they learned an adult man had shot Barnes with a rifle. Deputies took the suspect into custody and began providing emergency medical care to Barnes until St. Lucie County Fire District personnel arrived. Barnes was then taken to a local hospital, where he died.

Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division are continuing to process evidence and conduct interviews to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The suspect remains in custody.

Investigators say there is no threat to the public. The case remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man, 28, dies Tuesday after weekend shooting on South 14th Street
cards.teaser: A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was shot multiple times early Sunday morning in the 300 block of South 14th Street in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was shot multiple times in Fort Pierce over the weekend, according to police. The shooting happened early Sunday morning at about 3:43 a.m. in the 300 block of South 14th Street. Officers arrived at the scene and found two people with apparent gunshot wounds. The man sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was taken to a local hospital but died from his injuries on Tuesday. Officers also found a 28-year-old woman with injuries to her hand from the shooting, but her injuries were described as not life-threatening.

Police said a preliminary investigation indicated that the victims had been involved in an earlier altercation in the 5800 block of Okeechobee Road before returning to their residence. As they arrived home, a man believed to be involved in the previous altercation approached and opened fire before fleeing the area. Police said this investigation remains active and ongoing. The names of the victims have not been released. Anyone with information in the case is encouraged to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce rejects settlement in Little Jim's lawsuit, plans to revamp waterfront development process
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant. The rejection means more taxpayer dollars will likely go toward defending the case. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has an obligation to defend the lawsuit, adding that he feels the lawsuit doesn't have any merit. Broderick said the settlement wasn't practical, particularly a provision that would have required taxpayers to vote on future waterfront land decisions. Keene told WPTV he will continue the litigation and the fight.

The Little Jim's case is at least the fourth waterfront property dispute and the second to result in a lawsuit. In 2023, King's Landing developer Dale Matteson threatened legal action after claiming the city sold him buildable land filled with old power plant concrete. In 2024, Fisherman's Wharf developer Chris Shelli filed suit after state records showed the city promised property it didn't own. In 2025, Little Jim's land lease expired and the city sought bids to take over the property before abruptly canceling the process. The city became responsible for nearly $200,000 in unpaid rent tied to Crabby's Waterfront Restaurant this year. Broderick said the city is creating a new real estate management position to track leases, rent payments, and waterfront properties.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Clerk's website down for hours Tuesday due to third-party service issue
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday, redirecting visitors to another site before returning online by about 1:30 p.m.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller Michelle Miller posted a video on social media Tuesday afternoon addressing the website outage that redirected visitors to another site for hours. The website was back online by about 1:30 p.m. Miller said the website faced a temporary redirection issue caused by a third-party service provider. Miller assured the public that at no time was personal or confidential information compromised or at risk. The clerk's office does not store sensitive personal information on the public-facing website.

Jose Clavijo, the agency's IT director, said they received a report just before 8 a.m. that something was wrong with the county clerk's homepage. Clavijo said it was the absolute highest priority to get it fixed, and as soon as he identified the issue, he directed staff to turn it off and start the investigation. The clerk's office communications team said this wasn't a hack because there wasn't any personal information compromised. Residents could still access information and services on the website through direct links instead of using the homepage. Clavijo said payments, property fraud services and all other services remained accessible. Clavijo said the office is working to prevent similar issues from happening again and that as soon as the exact issue is identified, there will be a tremendous remediation.
